note:
The Analysis tab's verdict: the permitted range, the bracket chip, the sub-line that says why, and the population line in the foot. PR 4a. 4b's climb and findings rows are added to this file when they ship, rather than photographed empty here.

PRECONDITION, and it decides whether this sheet proves anything: the server must be running with ANALYSIS_TAB_ENABLED=true. The flag defaults OFF when unset, and a run against a server without it photographs a deck page with four tabs and no Analysis cell — which reads as coverage while proving nothing. The variable is `true` in the repo root `.env`, so a dev server started from a worktree that never copied `.env` is the way this goes wrong.

EVERY ROW REACHES THE SURFACE BY A PRESS, not by a URL. `BuilderTabs` is client state: the tab produces no address, and `builder-view.ts` says so in its own header. A URL sweep is exactly how the card mark shipped broken into the deck's card view, which is on record. So each row clicks the Analysis tab and then the invitation, and the profile costs 630ms median and up to 2.2s on the slowest real deck — which is what the settles are sized for, not padding.

ANALYSIS_DECK and ANALYSIS_SPLIT_DECK must be deck ids the SIGNED-IN account owns. A deck belonging to another account renders not-found, and the cell then photographs a 404 while counting as reached — which is how the first run of this file produced six cells of "THERE'S NO PAGE HERE". On `local-dev` the e2e account owns `d0000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000cafe` (permits [3], the exact reading) and `d0000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000beef` (a clean brew, permits [1,2]). Any deck draws a verdict: every reading here is a function of the permitted range, and `[1,2]` is the reading a clean deck gets rather than an empty state. What a single deck CANNOT photograph is the other four readings, so the split row names a second deck (ANALYSIS_SPLIT_DECK) whose cards reach a range — the chip, the second mark and the ringed `?` are drawn on that one alone, and a sheet without it photographs the exact reading twice.

NO `shares` BLOCK, deliberately. `check:shared` answers whether routes that are supposed to carry the same control do it by rendering the same component, and there is one mount here: `analysis-panel.tsx` renders `VerdictBlock` and nothing else does. A block naming it today would assert the share against every future row in this file — including 4b's climb and findings, which are different components — and fail them for being correct. It is owed the day a second surface is meant to draw the same head.

THE SPLIT FIXTURE IS TRIVIAL TO REBUILD and does not need a 99-card list: a deck whose cards carry no game changer, no mass land denial, no extra turn and no two-card combo permits `[1,2]`, and an EMPTY brew with a commander satisfies all four. That is the low range rather than the high one, which is the right one to photograph anyway — `[1,2]` and `[4,5]` share the chip, the second mark and the ringed `?`, and only `[1,2]` can be made without assembling a deck that is genuinely past three brackets.
